questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.ai_explanation: Altitude is a height measured from a reference level, so it has magnitude without a vector direction. Force, weight, displacement and acceleration are vectors.
questions.explanation: Altitude is a height measured from a reference level, so it has magnitude without a vector direction. Force, weight, displacement and acceleration are vectors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The force with which an object is attracted to the earth is called its
questions.ai_explanation: Weight is the gravitational force acting on an object: W = mg. Mass measures the amount of matter and is measured in kilograms; weight is measured in newtons.
questions.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force acting on an object: W = mg. Mass measures the amount of matter and is measured in kilograms; weight is measured in newtons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The refractive index of a liquid is 1.5. If the speed of light in a vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, the speed of light in the liquid is
questions.ai_explanation: Refractive index n = c/v, so v = c/n = (3.0 × 10⁸)/1.5 = 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Light travels more slowly in this liquid than in a vacuum.
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = c/v, so v = c/n = (3.0 × 10⁸)/1.5 = 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Light travels more slowly in this liquid than in a vacuum.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If the relative density of a metal is 19, what is the mass of 20 cm³ of the metal when immersed in water?
questions.ai_explanation: Relative density 19 means a density of 19 g/cm³. Mass = density × volume = 19 × 20 = 380 g. Immersion changes apparent weight, not the mass of the metal.
questions.explanation: Relative density 19 means a density of 19 g/cm³. Mass = density × volume = 19 × 20 = 380 g. Immersion changes apparent weight, not the mass of the metal.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about liquid pressure is NOT correct? The pressure

options.A: At a point in a liquid is proportional to the depth.
options.B: At any point in a liquid is the same at the same level.
options.C: Is exerted equally in all directions at any point.
options.D: Of a liquid at any point on the wall of its container acts in a direction perpendicular to the wall.
options.E: At a particular depth depends on the shape of the vessel.

questions.ai_explanation: For a liquid at rest, pressure due to the liquid is p = ρgh. At a given depth it depends on density and depth, not on the shape of the container.
questions.explanation: For a liquid at rest, pressure due to the liquid is p = ρgh. At a given depth it depends on density and depth, not on the shape of the container.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements about defects of vision are correct? I. For a long-sighted person, close objects appear blurred. II. For a short-sighted person, distant objects appear blurred. III. Short sight is corrected using converging lenses.
questions.ai_explanation: Long-sightedness makes close objects difficult to focus on; short-sightedness makes distant objects blurred. Short-sightedness is corrected using diverging lenses, so I and II are correct but III is false.
questions.explanation: Long-sightedness makes close objects difficult to focus on; short-sightedness makes distant objects blurred. Short-sightedness is corrected using diverging lenses, so I and II are correct but III is false.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The range of wavelengths of the visible spectrum is 400nm – 700nm. The wavelength of gamma rays is
questions.ai_explanation: Gamma rays have much shorter wavelengths than visible light. Their wavelengths are therefore shorter than 400 nm.
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have much shorter wavelengths than visible light. Their wavelengths are therefore shorter than 400 nm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If the pressure on 100 cm³ of an ideal gas is doubled while its kelvin temperature is halved, what is the new volume?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV/T is constant. V₂ = V₁(P₁/P₂)(T₂/T₁) = 100 × ½ × ½ = 25 cm³. Both changes reduce the volume.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV/T is constant. V₂ = V₁(P₁/P₂)(T₂/T₁) = 100 × ½ × ½ = 25 cm³. Both changes reduce the volume.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following arrangements in the sequence shown can be used to obtain a pure spectrum of white light?

options.A: Source, slit, converging lens, prism, converging lens, screen.
options.C: Source, converging lens, prism, diverging lens, screen.
options.D: Source, slit, prism, diverging lens, screen

questions.ai_explanation: The slit provides a narrow source. The first converging lens makes the rays parallel before the prism separates the colours; the second converging lens focuses them onto the screen to form a pure spectrum.
questions.explanation: The slit provides a narrow source. The first converging lens makes the rays parallel before the prism separates the colours; the second converging lens focuses them onto the screen to form a pure spectrum.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: It is usual to transmit electric power at high voltage and low current. Which of the following are possible advantages of the method. I Heat losses are reduced because the currents are small. II Thin wires can be used because small currents are flowing. III The power can flow faster because the voltage is high.
questions.ai_explanation: For a given transmitted power, a higher voltage requires a smaller current. Heating loss is I²R, so a smaller current reduces heating and allows a smaller conductor cross-section for the same loss limit. Higher voltage does not mean that power travels faster.
questions.explanation: For a given transmitted power, a higher voltage requires a smaller current. Heating loss is I²R, so a smaller current reduces heating and allows a smaller conductor cross-section for the same loss limit. Higher voltage does not mean that power travels faster.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The linear expansivity of brass is 2 × 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹. If a piece of brass has volume 10 cm³ at 0 °C, what is its volume at 100 °C?
questions.ai_explanation: For a solid, volume expansivity is approximately 3α. V = V₀(1 + 3αΔT) = 10(1 + 3 × 2 × 10⁻⁵ × 100) = 10.06 cm³.
questions.explanation: For a solid, volume expansivity is approximately 3α. V = V₀(1 + 3αΔT) = 10(1 + 3 × 2 × 10⁻⁵ × 100) = 10.06 cm³.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 24 V potential difference is applied across four 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel. What is the current in each resistor?
questions.ai_explanation: Each parallel branch has the full 24 V across it. The current in each 6 Ω resistor is I = V/R = 24/6 = 4 A. The total current through all four branches is 16 A.
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch has the full 24 V across it. The current in each 6 Ω resistor is I = V/R = 24/6 = 4 A. The total current through all four branches is 16 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The electrochemical equivalent of a metal is 0.126 × 10⁻⁶ kg/C. What mass of metal will a current of 5 A deposit from a suitable bath in 1 hour?
questions.ai_explanation: The charge passed is Q = It = 5 × 3600 = 18000 C. Deposited mass m = ZQ = 0.126 × 10⁻⁶ × 18000 = 2.268 × 10⁻³ kg.
questions.explanation: The charge passed is Q = It = 5 × 3600 = 18000 C. Deposited mass m = ZQ = 0.126 × 10⁻⁶ × 18000 = 2.268 × 10⁻³ kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Ripples on water are similar to light waves in that they both
questions.ai_explanation: Both water ripples and light can change direction through refraction and spread around edges or openings through diffraction. They do not need to have the same speed or wavelength to show these wave behaviours.
questions.explanation: Both water ripples and light can change direction through refraction and spread around edges or openings through diffraction. They do not need to have the same speed or wavelength to show these wave behaviours.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: 1000 identical drops of oil of density 500 kg/m³ have a total mass of 5 × 10⁻⁴ kg. One drop forms a thin film of area 0.5 m² on water. What is the film thickness?
questions.ai_explanation: One drop has mass (5 × 10⁻⁴)/1000 = 5 × 10⁻⁷ kg. Its volume is m/ρ = 10⁻⁹ m³. Film thickness = volume/area = 10⁻⁹/0.5 = 2 × 10⁻⁹ m.
questions.explanation: One drop has mass (5 × 10⁻⁴)/1000 = 5 × 10⁻⁷ kg. Its volume is m/ρ = 10⁻⁹ m³. Film thickness = volume/area = 10⁻⁹/0.5 = 2 × 10⁻⁹ m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A spring has total length 14 cm when a mass of 20 g is hung from it, and length 16 cm when a mass of 30 g is hung from it. Calculate the unstretched length, assuming Hooke’s law is obeyed.
questions.ai_explanation: Hooke’s law makes extension proportional to load. An extra 10 g increases the length by 2 cm, so the 20 g load produces a 4 cm extension. The natural length is 14 − 4 = 10 cm.
questions.explanation: Hooke’s law makes extension proportional to load. An extra 10 g increases the length by 2 cm, so the 20 g load produces a 4 cm extension. The natural length is 14 − 4 = 10 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is correct? I. Mass number equals the total number of protons and electrons in an atom. II. Atomic number equals the number of protons in an atom. III. The number of electrons in an atom equals the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
questions.ai_explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons, so II is correct. Mass number counts protons plus neutrons. A neutral atom has equal numbers of electrons and protons, not protons plus neutrons.
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons, so II is correct. Mass number counts protons plus neutrons. A neutral atom has equal numbers of electrons and protons, not protons plus neutrons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A current of 3 A flows for 10 seconds through a 20 Ω heating element embedded in 1000 g of oil, raising the oil temperature by 10 °C. Assuming the electrical energy heats the oil, what is its specific heat capacity?
questions.ai_explanation: Electrical energy supplied is I²Rt = 3² × 20 × 10 = 1800 J. Using Q = mcΔT, c = 1800/(1000 × 10) = 0.18 J/(g·°C), equivalent to 180 J/(kg·°C).
questions.explanation: Electrical energy supplied is I²Rt = 3² × 20 × 10 = 1800 J. Using Q = mcΔT, c = 1800/(1000 × 10) = 0.18 J/(g·°C), equivalent to 180 J/(kg·°C).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A cell has an open-circuit terminal voltage of 2.2 V. When a 4 Ω resistor is connected across it, the terminal voltage falls to 2.0 V. What is the internal resistance?
questions.ai_explanation: The current through the external resistor is I = 2/4 = 0.5 A. The internal voltage drop is 2.2 − 2.0 = 0.2 V, so internal resistance r = 0.2/0.5 = 0.40 Ω.
questions.explanation: The current through the external resistor is I = 2/4 = 0.5 A. The internal voltage drop is 2.2 − 2.0 = 0.2 V, so internal resistance r = 0.2/0.5 = 0.40 Ω.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the energy changes which take place when a steam engine drives a generator which lights a lamp?

options.C: Heat → kinetic energy → electricity → heat and light

questions.ai_explanation: The steam engine changes thermal energy into mechanical motion. The generator changes that motion into electrical energy, and the lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.
questions.explanation: The steam engine changes thermal energy into mechanical motion. The generator changes that motion into electrical energy, and the lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following may be used to determine relative humidity in a physics laboratory? I Manometer II Wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer III Hair hygrometer IV A hydrometer
questions.ai_explanation: A wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer uses evaporative cooling to determine humidity. A hair hygrometer uses the change in hair length with humidity. A manometer measures pressure; a hydrometer measures liquid density.
questions.explanation: A wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer uses evaporative cooling to determine humidity. A hair hygrometer uses the change in hair length with humidity. A manometer measures pressure; a hydrometer measures liquid density.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of light in a vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. If a transparent liquid has refractive index 4/3, what is the speed of light in the liquid?
questions.ai_explanation: The refractive index is n = c/v. Therefore v = (3.0 × 10⁸)/(4/3) = 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s.
questions.explanation: The refractive index is n = c/v. Therefore v = (3.0 × 10⁸)/(4/3) = 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A charge of 0.2 C experiences a force of 4 N in an electric field. What is the electric field strength?
questions.ai_explanation: Electric field strength is force per unit charge: E = F/q = 4/0.2 = 20 N/C.
questions.explanation: Electric field strength is force per unit charge: E = F/q = 4/0.2 = 20 N/C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Longitudinal waves do not exhibit
questions.ai_explanation: Polarization requires vibrations perpendicular to the direction of travel. Longitudinal waves vibrate along their direction of travel, so they cannot be polarized.
questions.explanation: Polarization requires vibrations perpendicular to the direction of travel. Longitudinal waves vibrate along their direction of travel, so they cannot be polarized.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The distance travelled by a particle starting from rest is plotted against the square of the time elapsed from the commencement of motion. The resulting graph is linear. The slope of this graph is a measure of
questions.ai_explanation: Starting from rest with constant acceleration, s = ½at². A graph of s against t² therefore has slope ½a. Equivalently, if s = kt², differentiating twice gives a = 2k.
questions.explanation: Starting from rest with constant acceleration, s = ½at². A graph of s against t² therefore has slope ½a. Equivalently, if s = kt², differentiating twice gives a = 2k.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental S.I. unit?
questions.ai_explanation: The radian measures plane angle and is a dimensionless derived unit. Metre, ampere, kelvin and second are SI base units.
questions.explanation: The radian measures plane angle and is a dimensionless derived unit. Metre, ampere, kelvin and second are SI base units.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For which quantities are the dimensions ML²T⁻² correct? I. Moment of a force. II. Work. III. Acceleration.
questions.ai_explanation: Force has dimensions MLT⁻². Both moment of force and work multiply force by a distance, giving ML²T⁻². Acceleration has dimensions LT⁻², so I and II are correct.
questions.explanation: Force has dimensions MLT⁻². Both moment of force and work multiply force by a distance, giving ML²T⁻². Acceleration has dimensions LT⁻², so I and II are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What volume of alcohol of density 8.4 × 10² kg/m³ has the same mass as 4.2 m³ of petrol of density 7.2 × 10² kg/m³?
questions.ai_explanation: The petrol mass is 720 × 4.2 = 3024 kg. For alcohol of density 840 kg/m³, volume = mass/density = 3024/840 = 3.6 m³.
questions.explanation: The petrol mass is 720 × 4.2 = 3024 kg. For alcohol of density 840 kg/m³, volume = mass/density = 3024/840 = 3.6 m³.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For correcting long sight defects in the human eye we require a
questions.ai_explanation: A long-sighted eye does not converge light from close objects sufficiently. A converging lens adds focusing power so that the image forms on the retina.
questions.explanation: A long-sighted eye does not converge light from close objects sufficiently. A converging lens adds focusing power so that the image forms on the retina.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a concave mirror to form a real diminished image, the object must be placed

options.B: Between the mirror and its focus
options.C: Between the focus and the centre of curvature
options.E: At a distance greater than the radius of curvature

questions.ai_explanation: A concave mirror forms a real, smaller image when the object is beyond its centre of curvature. The image then lies between the focus and the centre of curvature.
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms a real, smaller image when the object is beyond its centre of curvature. The image then lies between the focus and the centre of curvature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The unit of quantity of electricity (electric charge) is called
questions.ai_explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs. One coulomb is the charge transferred by a current of one ampere flowing for one second: Q = It.
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs. One coulomb is the charge transferred by a current of one ampere flowing for one second: Q = It.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The resistance of a wire depends on
questions.ai_explanation: For a uniform wire, R = ρL/A. Resistance depends on its length, cross-sectional area (and therefore diameter), and resistivity. Temperature also affects resistivity, so all four factors matter.
questions.explanation: For a uniform wire, R = ρL/A. Resistance depends on its length, cross-sectional area (and therefore diameter), and resistivity. Temperature also affects resistivity, so all four factors matter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 2 Ω, are connected in parallel with matching polarities. What current flows through an external 1 Ω resistor?
questions.ai_explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V, while their combined internal resistance is 2/2 = 1 Ω. Including the external resistor, I = 1.5/(1 + 1) = 0.75 A.
questions.explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V, while their combined internal resistance is 2/2 = 1 Ω. Including the external resistor, I = 1.5/(1 + 1) = 0.75 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which component is NOT contained in a zinc-carbon dry cell?
questions.ai_explanation: A zinc-carbon dry cell contains a carbon rod, a zinc casing and a paste containing ammonium chloride and manganese dioxide. A copper rod is not one of these components.
questions.explanation: A zinc-carbon dry cell contains a carbon rod, a zinc casing and a paste containing ammonium chloride and manganese dioxide. A copper rod is not one of these components.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following can be described as high tension transmission?
questions.ai_explanation: High-tension transmission means high-voltage transmission. For the same power, using a high voltage permits a low current and reduces I²R heating losses in the conductors.
questions.explanation: High-tension transmission means high-voltage transmission. For the same power, using a high voltage permits a low current and reduces I²R heating losses in the conductors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: All heat generated in a 5 Ω resistor by a 2 A current flowing for 30 seconds evaporates 5 g of liquid at its boiling point. What is the specific latent heat of the liquid?
questions.ai_explanation: The heat supplied is I²Rt = 2² × 5 × 30 = 600 J. Specific latent heat is energy per unit mass: L = 600/5 = 120 J/g.
questions.explanation: The heat supplied is I²Rt = 2² × 5 × 30 = 600 J. Specific latent heat is energy per unit mass: L = 600/5 = 120 J/g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a standing wave occurs in an air column, the distance between a node and its nearest antinode is equal to
questions.ai_explanation: In a standing wave, adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart. An antinode is midway between them, so a node and its nearest antinode are one-quarter wavelength apart.
questions.explanation: In a standing wave, adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart. An antinode is midway between them, so a node and its nearest antinode are one-quarter wavelength apart.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements are NOT correct? I. At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not affect the speed of sound in air treated as an ideal gas. II. The speed of sound in air increases with temperature. III. The quality of a note depends only on its frequency.
questions.ai_explanation: At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not change the ideal-gas speed of sound. Sound speed increases with temperature. The quality or timbre of a note depends on its mixture of frequencies and their relative amplitudes, so only III is incorrect.
questions.explanation: At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not change the ideal-gas speed of sound. Sound speed increases with temperature. The quality or timbre of a note depends on its mixture of frequencies and their relative amplitudes, so only III is incorrect.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two identical tuning forks have natural frequency 256 Hz. One is loaded, and 4 beats per second are heard when they sound together. What is the frequency of the loaded fork?
questions.ai_explanation: Adding a small load to a tuning fork lowers its frequency. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies, so the loaded fork vibrates at 256 − 4 = 252 Hz.
questions.explanation: Adding a small load to a tuning fork lowers its frequency. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies, so the loaded fork vibrates at 256 − 4 = 252 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Dew point is the temperature at which water vapour in the atmosphere

options.D: Is just sufficient to cause cooling
options.E: Has a relative humidity of fifty percent

questions.ai_explanation: The dew point is the temperature to which air must be cooled, without changing its water-vapour content, to become saturated and start forming liquid droplets.
questions.explanation: The dew point is the temperature to which air must be cooled, without changing its water-vapour content, to become saturated and start forming liquid droplets.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The lower (0 °C) and upper (100 °C) fixed points of a mercury-in-glass thermometer are 210 mm apart. In a room, the mercury ends 49 mm above the lower point. What is the room temperature to one decimal place?
questions.ai_explanation: The 210 mm interval represents 100 °C. A rise of 49 mm therefore corresponds to (49/210) × 100 = 23.33… °C, or 23.3 °C to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The 210 mm interval represents 100 °C. A rise of 49 mm therefore corresponds to (49/210) × 100 = 23.33… °C, or 23.3 °C to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If a solid changes directly into a gas when heat is applied the process is called
questions.ai_explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through a liquid phase. Dry ice is a familiar example.
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through a liquid phase. Dry ice is a familiar example.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Heat is supplied at 100 W to 1.0 × 10⁻² kg of liquid for 20 seconds. Its temperature rises by 5 °C. Assuming the supplied heat warms the liquid, what is its specific heat capacity?
questions.ai_explanation: Heat supplied is Pt = 100 × 20 = 2000 J. The temperature rise is 5 K, so c = Q/(mΔT) = 2000/(0.01 × 5) = 4.0 × 10⁴ J/(kg·K).
questions.explanation: Heat supplied is Pt = 100 × 20 = 2000 J. The temperature rise is 5 K, so c = Q/(mΔT) = 2000/(0.01 × 5) = 4.0 × 10⁴ J/(kg·K).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a model atmosphere, sea-level pressure is 10⁵ N/m², density is uniform at 1 kg/m³, and g = 10 m/s². What is the height of this atmosphere?
questions.ai_explanation: For the stated uniform-density model, p = ρgh. Hence h = 10⁵/(1 × 10) = 10000 m. This is the height of the simplified model atmosphere.
questions.explanation: For the stated uniform-density model, p = ρgh. Hence h = 10⁵/(1 × 10) = 10000 m. This is the height of the simplified model atmosphere.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct explanation of the inertia of a body?

options.A: Ability to overcome the earth’s gravity
options.D: Reluctance to start moving and its readiness to stop moving once it has begun to move
options.E: Reluctance to start moving and its reluctance to stop moving once it has begun to move.

questions.ai_explanation: Inertia is resistance to a change in velocity. A body tends to stay at rest or continue moving with constant velocity unless a resultant external force acts.
questions.explanation: Inertia is resistance to a change in velocity. A body tends to stay at rest or continue moving with constant velocity unless a resultant external force acts.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A water pump at Kainji Dam lifts 1000 kg of water through a vertical height of 10 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its useful lifting power?
questions.ai_explanation: The gain in gravitational potential energy is mgh = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 100000 J. Dividing by 10 s gives 10000 W = 10 kW of useful lifting power.
questions.explanation: The gain in gravitational potential energy is mgh = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 100000 J. Dividing by 10 s gives 10000 W = 10 kW of useful lifting power.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What is the apparent colour of a RED SHIRT when viewed in PURE green light?
questions.ai_explanation: In the ideal colour model, a red shirt reflects red light and absorbs green light. Under pure green illumination there is no red light to reflect, so it appears black.
questions.explanation: In the ideal colour model, a red shirt reflects red light and absorbs green light. Under pure green illumination there is no red light to reflect, so it appears black.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which list gives the colours of the visible spectrum in order from longest to shortest wavelength?

options.A: Blue, red, green. Yellow, indigo, violet, orange.
options.B: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.
options.C: Red, orange, yellow, indigo, green, blue, violet.
options.D: Indigo, green, blue, violet, yellow, red, orange.
options.E: Yellow, blue, green, violet, orange, indigo, red.

questions.ai_explanation: From longest to shortest visible wavelength, the usual order is red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. Frequency increases in the reverse direction to wavelength.
questions.explanation: From longest to shortest visible wavelength, the usual order is red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. Frequency increases in the reverse direction to wavelength.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Cathode rays are
questions.ai_explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. They carry negative charge and can be deflected by electric and magnetic fields.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. They carry negative charge and can be deflected by electric and magnetic fields.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Radio waves travel at 3 × 10⁸ m/s. A station broadcasts at 800 kHz. What is the wavelength?
questions.ai_explanation: Convert 800 kHz to 800000 Hz. Wavelength λ = v/f = (3 × 10⁸)/800000 = 375 m.
questions.explanation: Convert 800 kHz to 800000 Hz. Wavelength λ = v/f = (3 × 10⁸)/800000 = 375 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What does it cost to run five 50 W lamps and four 100 W lamps for 10 hours at a tariff of 2 kobo per kWh?
questions.ai_explanation: Total power is 5 × 50 + 4 × 100 = 650 W = 0.65 kW. In 10 hours the lamps use 6.5 kWh. At the stated rate, the cost is 6.5 × 2 = 13 kobo = ₦0.13.
questions.explanation: Total power is 5 × 50 + 4 × 100 = 650 W = 0.65 kW. In 10 hours the lamps use 6.5 kWh. At the stated rate, the cost is 6.5 × 2 = 13 kobo = ₦0.13.
